parent.acceptance: accepted fixed-seed two-position active parallel source

model.repair: unchanged parent half-hour direct system CM, after failure affects mission outcome

hypotheses_to_test_natively: Both arms record identical POS-A and POS-B failure-mode times and identities before their first mission-outcome divergence; this is an intended comparability hypothesis, not an assumed result.
The active 1/3 arm remains functional after both configured positions fail while POS-C is up, and completes the long mission at hour 34.
The active 2/3 arm remains functional after the first branch failure but aborts its mission when a second distinct branch fails before repair.
Each recorded repair and status interval is reconciled from native events and half-hour report bins; no aggregate metric alone proves the threshold.
acceptance_gates: parent and both source fingerprints, exact table-level delta, manual/dictionary/executable fingerprints
session-0 SSH, host-wide native mutex, GUI PID 13340 identity, unique run directories
native import/export/calc/report and exact authored row-table roundtrip with zero conversion errors
read-only author and independent event-level review of failures, threshold transitions, mission outcome, repair and report bins
raw invocation, logs, model, report and closure files hashed in an evidence index
limits: Single fixed seed and one repetition cannot establish population reliability.
This pair does not test POS-C failure, alternate branch rates, nonzero switching time, passive operation, online maintenance, QTYPB greater than one, nested RBD, GUI RBD view or cross-engine parity.
If the native engine changes failure samples between arms, the event-level contrast must be reframed or rejected rather than claiming a paired threshold test.
